newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to return dealer status to several banks.
newsitem.headline: Romania to return dealer status to several banks.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) will reauthorise several banks to act as dealers on the local foreign exchange market, in a move to liberalise the market, a BNR official said.
The foreign exchange market operates at present with only four dealers.
"Several banks will get back their local dealer licences starting next Tuesday," director Adrian Vasilescu, a spokesman for the BNR, told Reuters late on Friday.
Vasilescu did not elaborate on the move, saying the BNR had yet to decide which of the around 30 banks operating on the Romanian market would get back their lost dealer status.
"At this stage I can't name those banks," Vasilescu said.
The move will end almost one year of foreign exchange curbs imposed by the former leftist governemnt last March when it stripped all but four banks of their local dealer licence.
Except for the four, the other banks had to operate as brokers and had to observe rates imposed by the four dealers.
Since March 1996, trading stalled on the interbank market with operators repeatedly demanding the BNR reconsider the move and restore their local dealer licences.
The International Monetary Fund cited the restrictions on the foreign exchange market among the main reasons behind its decision to suspend vital loans for Romania in 1996.
Liberalising the foreign exchange market is part of a reform programme initiated by the new centrist coalition government headed by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea.

On Friday, Ciorbea said talks with the IMF and other international lenders on renewed financing have almost come to an end. He is expected to present the outcome of the talks along with the detailed reform programme next Monday.
